source.title: Algorithmic Regularization in Over-parameterized Matrix Sensing and Neural Networks with Quadratic Activations
source.authors: Yuanzhi Li; Tengyu Ma; Hongyang Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on over-parameterized matrix sensing and quadratic neural networks. They refine the scope of generalization claims by showing that initialization, parameterization, and training method affect the training–test gap, but do not test any listed version's specific behavior.
record.gate_note: The study does not test arbitrary-label memorization followed by generalization on natural labels, or the specific width, convolution, optimizer-comparison, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example claims. Its simulations report generalization outcomes on synthetic matrix sensing and quadratic-network tasks; cited findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves recovery guarantees and reports synthetic matrix-sensing and quadratic-network experiments. None tests V1–V8: there is no random-label comparison, width sweep, architectural comparison on images, adaptive-optimizer comparison, controlled batch-budget comparison, dropout experiment, sharpness measurement, or memorized-example removal. Related generalization results do not justify T5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish implicit regularization for over-parameterized matrix sensing under RIP and small initialization, and extend the analysis to quadratic networks using truncation and explicit rescaling. Their simulations demonstrate initialization and parameterization effects. Extending these guarantees to deeper networks with other activations and losses remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and simulates synthetic matrix sensing and quadratic-activation networks, not the natural-label image or language tasks in the listed versions. The neural-network algorithm includes a truncation and an explicit rescaling step; standard gradient descent is used for matrix sensing.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization size changes the training–test gap; factorized versus projected optimization changes test error; the reported SGD comparison uses a large initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller initialization narrows the training–test error gap; with alpha=1, training error falls below 10^-4 while test error remains of order 10^-1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization magnitude affects generalization in the studied factorized matrix-sensing model.

fits_no_version.finding: With initialization 0.01 times the identity, test error continues decreasing through 10^5 iterations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-initialization matrix-sensing runs can sustain improving test recovery over extended training.

fits_no_version.finding: Factorized gradient descent recovers the target more accurately than projected gradient descent onto the PSD cone in the tested sample regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameterization affects implicit regularization and test recovery in synthetic matrix sensing.

fits_no_version.finding: With identity initialization, both SGD and GD reach training error around 10^-7 or lower while test error remains large.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large initialization can permit interpolation without accurate test recovery in the reported quadratic-network setting.

record.problems: The experiments are limited to synthetic matrix-sensing and quadratic-network settings. Most plotted values are not given numerically in the text. The initialization comparison reports three-run means and error bars, but the plotted error-bar values are not stated. The neural-network theory relies on a modified algorithm with truncation and rescaling.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error changes as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning and the specified recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout effects across data sizes and strengths, including augmentation and weight-decay interactions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and rankings against other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row links to none; this does not dispute the reported experimental trends. Citations to original claim sources supply background, not tests of their specific claims.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and natural-label held-out performance in the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on image or language benchmarks.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and comparison with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.value: The gap between training and test error narrows as α decreases.

rows.note: The text describes the trend; plotted numeric values are not stated.
rows.check: The initialization trend is correctly reported but measures no listed version. Iterations should be 10^4, not 104. Section 6 defines normalized root training error and relative Frobenius recovery error as test error.
